Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Absolutely! Here's a simple breakdown of the main spirit categories:
Whiskey Family (the biggest category)
Bourbon: American whiskey made with at least 51% corn — smooth, slightly sweet, with vanilla and caramel notes. Great for beginners.
Scotch: Whiskey made in Scotland — often smoky or peaty, more complex flavors. All Scotch is whiskey, but not all whiskey is Scotch.
Rye: Made with rye grain — spicier and bolder than bourbon
Other Popular Spirits
Tequila: Made from agave in Mexico — earthy, citrusy, ranges from smooth to bold
Rum: Made from sugarcane or molasses — slightly sweet, smooth finish, great in cocktails or enjoyed on its own
Vodka: Neutral, subtle flavor — the most versatile for mixing, low-calorie option
Gin: Flavored with botanicals (juniper, citrus, herbs) — crisp and aromatic
We carry over 20,000 spirits from around the world, from well-known classics to rare craft bottles.
Which of these sounds most appealing to you? If you like sweeter, smoother flavors, bourbon or rum might be your starting point. If you prefer something lighter for cocktails, vodka or gin could be perfect.

Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Good question! The bourbon itself is all you really need, but here are a few simple things that will enhance your experience:
The Essentials (you probably already have these):
A glass — any tumbler or rocks glass works fine. For the best tasting experience, a tulip-shaped glass like a Glencairn concentrates the aromas, but it's not required when starting out.
Water — keep spring water or soft tap water handy. Adding a splash can soften the alcohol and release more flavors. Alternate sips of water and bourbon to cleanse your palate.
Ice (optional) — if you prefer bourbon "on the rocks," use big cubes or spheres that melt slower so your bourbon stays chilled without getting watered down.
How to drink it:
Start by trying it neat (no ice, no water) to taste the bourbon's true character. Then experiment with a splash of water or over ice to see what you prefer. There's no wrong way!

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Great question! Here's exactly how to taste bourbon properly for the first time:
Step 1: Pour & Observe
Pour about 1-2 ounces into a glass (any tumbler works fine). Start neat — no ice, no water — so you can experience the bourbon's true character.
Step 2: Smell First (This is Key!)
Gently bring the glass up to your nose — don't rush this step! You don't want to overwhelm your nose. Tilt the glass to one side and really get your nose in there. Give it a little swirl. Take your nose away after each sniff, then repeat. The first thing you smell is usually right — trust it. You'll notice layers revealing themselves: caramel, vanilla, maybe some spice.
Step 3: Take a Small Sip
Don't gulp — sip it slowly. Let it sit on your tongue for a moment before swallowing. Notice the flavors and how it feels.
Step 4: Experiment
After your first neat taste, try adding a splash of water — this actually releases more flavors and softens the alcohol punch. Or try it over ice if you prefer it chilled.
Pro tip: Have water on hand to alternate sips and cleanse your palate between tastes.
There's no wrong way — just explore and see what you enjoy! Ready to checkout and get started?
